• Revoke ALL active session refresh tokens globally
• Enforce 15-minute ephemeral token lifetimes
• Run cryptographic verification on loaded eBPF programs
• Rotate identity provider root signing keys

[Post 5/5]
5/5 We have synthesized the full threat package into an executive brief, slide presentation, and technical advisory checklist for engineering leads. Stay fortified.

Team Name – BRUTEFORCES

Team Id -

Problem Statement ID – 26154

Category – Software

Problem Statement Title

Gen AI Platform for Automated Content Transformation

Description

• Background Organisations frequently need to convert information available in different forms such as news articles, reports, advisories, threat intelligence, policy documents, research papers, announcements, incident reports or free-form prompts into specific communication artefacts suitable for various purposes. The process of manually analysing the source content, understanding the desired objective and creating the required output format is time-consuming, resource-intensive and often requires expertise in content creation, communication and domain knowledge.

There is a need for an intelligent platform that can transform user-provided content into a desired output format through a simple and configurable interface.
• Description The system shall act as an AI-powered content transformation engine that converts a common source of information into the specific deliverable requested by the operator, thereby reducing manual effort, improving consistency, accelerating content creation and enhancing operational efficiency.

The platform shall provide a dashboard through which an operator can submit source content in the form of high quality English language text, documents, articles, reports, prompts, images, videos or contextual information. In addition to providing the source content, the operator shall select one or more desired output types through configurable parameters available on the dashboard.

Based on the submitted content and the selected output type(s), the platform shall analyze the input, understand the context and intent, and generate the requested output artefact. The platform should support multiple output formats and allow operators to control generation parameters such as target audience, tone, language, level of detail, communication objective and content style.

In sum

mary, platform shall generate output corresponding to the option(s) selected by the operator on the dashboard.
• Examples include
• If 'Video' is selected, generate a complete video package including script, storyboard, scene descriptions, narration text, subtitles and visual recommendations.
• If 'LinkedIn Post' is selected, generate a professional LinkedIn post suitable for publication.
• If 'Twitter/X Post' is selected, generate platform-optimized tweets or tweet threads.
• If 'Advisory' is selected, generate a structured advisory document.
• If 'Infographic' is selected, generate infographic content, layout recommendations and key messaging.
• If 'Executive Summary' is selected, generate a concise executive briefing.
• If 'Presentation' is selected, generate presentation slides and speaker notes.
• If multiple output formats are selected, generate all selected deliverables from the same source content.
• Expected Solution/Deliverables for Evaluation
• Source Code Link (GitHub/Drive Link)
• Readme with Setup Instructions
• Architecture Document (Max 2 Pages)
• Demo Video (Max 2 Minutes)
• Technical Presentation (Max 5 Slides)

ABSTRACT

The Fake Review Classification System is a data-driven application developed to demonstrate the practical use of Natural Language Processing and machine learning techniques in identifying misleading product reviews on e-commerce platforms. In real-world online shopping environments such as Amazon and Flipkart, customers often depend on reviews before purchasing products. However, fake or manipulated reviews can mislead users, reduce trust, and affect buying decisions. This project aims to address these challenges by automatically detecting fake reviews accurately, thereby improving customer confidence and platform reliability.

The system utilizes historical review data such as review text content, writing patterns, repeated words, promotional language, and sentiment-based indicators to classify reviews as genuine or fake. A Logistic Regression model is applied to analyse the relationship between textual features and review authenticity, enabling the system to predict suspicious reviews effectively. TF-IDF vectorization is used to convert textual reviews into numerical features, allowing accurate and efficient classification based on past data patterns.

The application provides functionalities such as dataset input, text preprocessing, fake review prediction, confidence score generation, suspicious pattern explanation, and performance evaluation through confusion matrix and classification reports. These features help customers make better purchase decisions and assist e-commerce platforms in filtering deceptive content, maintaining review quality, and improving trustworthiness.

This project highlights the real-world appl

ication of machine learning techniques like Logistic Regression, combined with efficient text processing and algorithmic design, to solve practical problems in digital commerce. The Fake Review Classification System closely resembles modern intelligent review monitoring systems used in the industry, where maintaining trust and preventing manipulation are essential. In conclusion, this project bridges theoretical concepts with practical implementation, offering valuable insights into predictive analytics, text mining, and intelligent software system design.

GENERAL OVERVIEW

In the present era of digital transformation, data-driven decision-making has become an essential component across various domains, including education, healthcare, business, and e-commerce. One such domain where intelligent decision-making plays a crucial role is online shopping platforms. E-commerce websites serve millions of customers daily, and maintaining the authenticity of product reviews is a challenging task due to the increasing volume of user-generated content.

Product reviews on e-commerce platforms are not always genuine and may vary significantly in quality and reliability due to multiple influencing factors such as promotional activities, paid reviewers, competitor manipulation, spam content, fake ratings, and misleading feedback. For instance, some sellers may post overly positive reviews to increase product sales, while others may submit negative reviews to damage competing products. Such practices affect customer trust and decision-making.

Traditionally, customers rely on star ratings and written reviews to decide whether to purchase a product. While this approach may work in simple scenarios, it often fails to identify deceptive or manipulated reviews. As a result, customers may purchase low-quality products based on fake positive reviews, while genuine products may lose reputation because of false negative feedback.

Fake reviews are not

only a business issue but also a trust and ethical concern. Misleading reviews create unfair competition, reduce transparency, and negatively impact the credibility of online marketplaces. Therefore, there is a growing need for intelligent systems that can automatically detect suspicious reviews and maintain review authenticity.

To address these challenges, the Fake Review Classification System is developed using machine learning techniques. This system leverages historical review data and predictive algorithms to classify reviews as genuine or fake accurately. By analysing review text, identifying suspicious writing patterns, and applying classification models, the system can provide reliable predictions regarding review authenticity.

In addition to classification, the system offers visualization features such as confusion matrix graphs and performance reports, which help users understand model accuracy and prediction results easily. It also provides explanations for suspicious reviews, such as promotional words, repeated phrases, short generic comments, and excessive punctuation, enabling better transparency in predictions.

This project not only improves customer confidence and platform reliability but also supports fair digital commerce practices by reducing misleading content. It serves as a practical example of how machine learning can be applied to solve real-world problems effectively.

1.2 OBJECTIVES

The primary objective of this project is to design and implement an intelligent system that detects fake product reviews using machine learning techniques. The system aims to enhance customer trust, improve decision-making, and maintain authenticity in e-commerce platforms.

The specific objectives of the project are as follows:

1 To collect and analyse historical product review data to understand patterns of genuine and fake reviews.

To identify key factors that influence review authenticity, such as promotional language, repeated words, short comments, a

nd suspicious writing patterns.

To preprocess the dataset by handling missing values, removing inconsistencies, and transforming review text into a suitable format.

To implement a classification-based machine learning model for detecting fake and genuine reviews.

To evaluate the performance of the model using appropriate metrics and ensure prediction accuracy.

To visualize the predicted results using graphical representations such as confusion matrix and performance reports.

To develop a system that provides confidence scores and explanations for suspicious reviews.

To reduce the impact of misleading reviews and improve fairness in online marketplaces.

To improve the efficiency of e-commerce review management through data-driven decision-making.

To provide a scalable solution that can be extended with advanced techniques in the future.

1.3 SCOPE

The scope of the proposed Fake Review Classification System encompasses both functional capabilities and academic significance, providing a comprehensive framework for practical implementation. The system is designed not only to solve real-world problems related to fake review detection and review authenticity analysis but also to demonstrate the effective application of machine learning and natural language processing techniques in a structured and scalable manner.

FUNCTIONAL SCOPE:

The functional scope of the system focuses on developing an intelligent and data-driven solution for detecting fake reviews in an e-commerce environment. The system is capable of collecting, processing, and analyzing historical product review data to generate accurate classification results. The key functionalities of the system include data acquisition, preprocessing, model training, prediction, visualization, and explanation generation.

Based on the trained model, the system predicts whether a new review is genuine or fake, enabling customers and e-commerce platforms to make better decisions. Additionally, the system provides visu

al representations of prediction performance through graphs and confusion matrix charts, making it easier for users to interpret the results.

Another important functionality is the explanation feature, which identifies suspicious indicators such as overly promotional words, repeated phrases, short generic comments, and excessive punctuation. This helps in improving transparency, reducing misleading content, and enhancing overall trust in online review systems.

EDUCATIONAL SCOPE:

From an academic perspective, this project serves as a valuable learning platform for students in the field of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and natural language processing. It provides hands-on experience in various stages of the machine learning pipeline, including data collection, preprocessing, feature extraction, model development, and evaluation.

Students gain a deeper understanding of classification algorithms and their applications in real-world scenarios such as fake review detection in e-commerce platforms. The project also enhances knowledge in text mining and data visualization techniques, enabling students to represent complex information in a simplified manner.

Furthermore, the project encourages analytical thinking and problem-solving skills, as students learn to identify suspicious review patterns, interpret prediction results, and improve model performance. It bridges the gap between theoretical concepts and practical implementation.

LIMITATIONS:

Despite its effectiveness, the system has certain limitations that must be considered. The accuracy of the model heavily depends on the quality, size, and diversity of the dataset. If the dataset is limited, imbalanced, or contains noisy and incorrect labels, the predictions may not be highly reliable.

The current system is based on Logistic Regression, which may not capture highly complex linguistic patterns and contextual meanings present in review text. Although effective for structured text classification, i

t may perform lower than advanced deep learning models on complex datasets. Additionally, the system does not incorporate real-time review streams, which may affect its adaptability to newly emerging spam patterns.

External factors such as reviewer behaviour, account credibility, verified purchase status, star ratings, and coordinated spam campaigns are not considered in the current model, which may influence review authenticity detection.

FUTURE ENHANCEMENT:

The system can be further enhanced by incorporating advanced technologies and features. Future improvements may include the integration of real-time review collection systems, enabling continuous updates and more accurate fake review detection.

Advanced machine learning models such as LSTM networks, XGBoost, and transformer-based models like BERT can be implemented to capture complex language patterns and improve classification accuracy. The system can also be developed into a web-based or mobile application, providing easy access and user interaction for customers and administrators.

Integration with databases such as MongoDB or cloud-based storage solutions can improve data management and scalability. Additionally, incorporating external factors such as reviewer history, star ratings, verified purchase status, user behaviour patterns, and multilingual reviews can further enhance the detection capability of the system.

CHAPTER 2

SYSTEM ANALYSIS

2.1 EXISTING SYSTEM

In traditional e-commerce review management systems, fake review detection is primarily carried out using manual moderation techniques or simple rule-based filtering methods. These methods rely on human inspection or basic keyword checks rather than systematic data analysis. While such approaches may identify some suspicious reviews, they are often inaccurate and inconsistent due to the large volume and dynamic nature of online reviews.

One of the major drawbacks of the existing system is the lack of data-driven decision-making. Historical

review data, which could provide valuable insights into fake review patterns, is either underutilized or completely ignored. As a result, the system fails to capture trends, deceptive writing styles, and variations in suspicious review behaviour.

Fake positive or negative reviews are a common issue in the existing system, leading to misleading product ratings and reduced customer trust. This not only results in poor purchase decisions but also creates unfair competition among sellers. On the other hand, genuine reviews may sometimes be incorrectly removed, causing inconvenience to honest customers and vendors.

Another limitation is the absence of automation in many review monitoring processes. Many decisions are made manually, increasing the chances of human error and reducing efficiency. The system also lacks effective visualization tools, making it difficult to analyze review authenticity trends and model performance.

Furthermore, the existing system does not consider important external factors such as reviewer behaviour history, verified purchase status, rating-text mismatch, coordinated spam activities, and multilingual review content, all of which significantly influence review authenticity.

2.2 PROPOSED SYSTEM

The proposed system introduces a machine learning-based approach to overcome the limitations of traditional methods. It utilizes historical review data and classification algorithms to detect fake reviews in an accurate and efficient manner.

The system follows a structured workflow consisting of data collection, preprocessing, feature extraction, model training, prediction, explanation generation, and visualization. Each stage is carefully designed to ensure data integrity and model performance.

One of the key strengths of the proposed system is its ability to process large volumes of review data and identify hidden suspicious patterns that are not easily detectable through manual analysis. The classification model establishes relationships betwee

n textual features and review authenticity, enabling precise predictions.

The system also incorporates visualization techniques such as confusion matrix graphs and performance reports to present the results in an intuitive manner. These visualizations help users understand model accuracy, prediction trends, and system effectiveness.

Additionally, the system provides explanations for suspicious reviews based on promotional words, repeated phrases, short generic comments, and excessive punctuation. This feature enhances transparency, improves trust, and helps users understand why a review is classified as fake.

Overall, the proposed system offers a reliable, efficient, and scalable solution for fake review classification in e-commerce platforms.

2.3 FEATURES

The proposed system includes several advanced features that enhance its functionality and usability:

Data Analysis: Processes large volumes of historical review data to identify suspicious trends and writing patterns.

Prediction Model: Uses classification algorithms for accurate fake review detection.

Visualization: Displays results through graphical representations such as confusion matrix and performance metrics.

Explanation System: Provides reasons for suspicious reviews such as promotional words, repeated phrases, short comments, and excessive punctuation.

User-Friendly Interface: Simple and easy-to-use system for review analysis and prediction.

Trust Improvement: Reduces misleading reviews and improves customer confidence in e-commerce platforms.

Scalability: Can be extended with advanced models, multilingual support, and real-time detection technologies.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE

3.1 SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE

proposed system is designed using a modular and layered architecture that ensures efficient data flow, scalability, and maintainability. The architecture consists of multiple interconnected components, each responsible for a specific function in fake review detection and review authenticit

y analysis.

The architecture begins with the data collection layer, where historical product review data is gathered. This data includes attributes such as review text, review labels, ratings, and related review information. The collected data serves as the foundation for the entire system and directly influences the accuracy of classification results.

The next stage is the data preprocessing layer, where raw review data is cleaned and prepared for analysis. In this stage, missing values are handled, duplicate entries are removed, unwanted symbols are filtered, and inconsistencies are corrected. Text normalization techniques such as lowercasing and stop word removal are also applied. Data preprocessing ensures that the dataset is reliable and suitable for machine learning operations.

Following preprocessing, the system performs feature engineering, which is a critical step in improving model performance. Features such as keywords, repeated phrases, word frequency patterns, and n-gram representations are selected and converted into numerical values using TF-IDF for model compatibility.

The model learns patterns and relationships between textual features and review authenticity. This trained model forms the core component responsible for prediction.

The predicted results are then processed in the visualization module, where graphical representations such as confusion matrix charts and performance reports are generated. These visualizations help users easily understand classification accuracy, trends, and system effectiveness.

ly, the system includes an explanation module, which identifies suspicious indicators such as promotional words, repeated phrases, short generic comments, and excessive punctuation. Overall, the system architecture ensures a smooth and logical flow of data from input to output, enabling accurate fake review detection and efficient decision-making. The modular design also allows easy scalability and future enhancements.

3.1.1 DESCRIPTION

The The proposed system operates through a well-defined sequence of stages, ensuring efficient data processing and accurate fake review classification. Each stage in the architecture plays a crucial role in transforming raw review data into meaningful insights for decision-making.

The process begins with the data collection stage, where historical product review data is gathered either manually through a user input portal or from external sources such as e-commerce platforms and review datasets. This data forms the foundation of the system and is critical for training the machine learning model.

To ensure data security and controlled usage, an access control mechanism is incorporated into the system. This feature restricts unauthorized access and ensures that only authorized users can interact with the system and view sensitive data.

Overall, the system follows a structured an

d logical workflow, transforming raw review data into actionable insights. The modular design of the architecture ensures flexibility, scalability, and ease of maintenance, allowing future enhancements such as integration with real-time review streams, multilingual support, and advanced deep learning models.

CHAPTER 4

SYSTEM IMPLEMENTATION

4.1 DATASET DESCRIPTION

The dataset used in this project plays a crucial role in determining the performance and accuracy of the machine learning model. It consists of historical records of product reviews collected from e-commerce sources over a specific period. This dataset serves as the foundation for training and testing the fake review classification model.

The dataset includes multiple attributes that represent different aspects of review authenticity patterns. These attributes are carefully selected to capture the variations in genuine and fake reviews influenced by writing style, sentiment, and suspicious behaviour. The primary attributes present in the dataset are:

Review Text: Represents the written feedback provided by users for a product. This helps in identifying linguistic patterns and suspicious content.

Label: Indicates whether the review is genuine or fake. This is the target variable used for classification.

Rating: Represents the star rating given by the reviewer, which may help in identifying rating-text inconsistencies.

Review Length: Represents the number of words or characters in a review, which may indicate short generic or unusually long suspicious reviews.

In addition to these attributes, derived features may also be included to enhance model performance. These include repeated words, promotional keywords, punctuation frequency, sentiment indicators, and n-gram patterns extracted from review text.

The dataset is stored in a structured format such as CSV (Comma Separated Values), which allows easy manipulation and processing using Python libraries like Pandas. A well-structured dataset ensures e

fficient data handling and improves the accuracy of results.

FIGURE 4.1: SAMPLE DATASET STRUCTURE

4.2 DATASET PREPROCESSING

Data preprocessing is one of the most critical stages in the machine learning pipeline. Raw review data collected from real-world environments is often incomplete, inconsistent, and noisy. Therefore, it must be processed and cleaned before being used for model training.

The preprocessing phase involves several steps:

1. DATA CLEANING

Missing values are identified and handled appropriately. In this project, records containing null or empty review text are removed. Unwanted symbols, special characters, extra spaces, and irrelevant content such as URLs are also eliminated from the review text to improve data quality.

2. REMOVING DUPLICATES

Duplicate review records are eliminated to avoid redundancy and bias in the dataset. Duplicate data can negatively impact model performance by causing overfitting and misleading predictions.

3. DATA TRANSFORMATION

Categorical variables such as review labels are converted into numerical format for machine learning compatibility. In this project, Genuine Reviews (CG) are converted to 0, and Fake Reviews (OR) are converted to 1. Review text is transformed into numerical feature vectors using TF-IDF vectorization.

4. TEXT NORMALIZATION

Text normalization is applied to standardize the review content. This includes converting all text into lowercase, removing stopwords, and reducing unnecessary variations in writing style. This ensures consistency across the dataset and improves feature extraction quality.

5. DATA SPLITTING

The dataset is divided into training and testing sets. The training dataset is used to train the machine learning model, while the testing dataset is used to evaluate its performance. In this project, 80% of the data is used for training and 20% for testing.

sed machine learning technique used for classification tasks. It establishes a relationship between input variables (independent variables) and the probability of belonging to a particular class. In this project, it is used to classify reviews as genuine or fake.

4.4 MODULE DESCRIPTION

To ensure high performance, maintainability, and scalability, the Fake Review Detection System is designed using a modular architecture. The system is divided into four primary functional modules, each responsible for a specific phase of the text classification pipeline, seamlessly transforming raw user input into meaningful predictions.

1. Data Acquisition and Packet Sniffing Module

This foundational module acts as the entry point of the system, responsible for collecting review data from external sources such as CSV datasets or user input. It ensures proper data formatting by selecting relevant columns and handles missing or inconsistent values through preprocessing steps like null removal

. This module guarantees that only clean and structured data is forwarded to the next stage.

2. Flow Aggregation and Feature Extraction Module

Raw textual data is unstructured and not directly suitable for machine learning, so this module converts it into a structured numerical format. It begins with text cleaning—lowercasing, removing URLs, special characters, and stopwords using NLTK. The cleaned text is then transformed into numerical feature vectors using TF-IDF, capturing the importance of relevant words and phrases and making the data machine-understandable.

3. Threat Classification (Machine Learning) Module

Cybersecurity SOC Incident-Response

Copilot

Name : Prem M     Roll No : 24ALR044

Problem Statement

Security Operations Center (SOC) teams receive large volumes of security alerts from endpoints, networks, cloud services and security tools. Analysts may struggle to quickly understand incidents, identify their severity, correlate related alerts, investigate indicators of compromise and determine the appropriate response actions.

How It Helps the Business or Public Organisation

The solution can help security teams reduce alert-investigation time, prioritize critical incidents and provide analysts with structured investigation and response guidance. It can improve consistency in incident handling while allowing human analysts to remain responsible for final security decisions.

Problem It Solves

It addresses alert overload, slow manual investigation, fragmented security information, difficulty correlating multiple alerts and inconsistent incident-response procedures. It also helps junior analysts understand security events and follow standardized investigation workflows.

Proposed GenAI Solution

Build a RAG-based SOC Incident-Response Copilot over a controlled knowledge base containing fictional or publicly available security policies, incident-response playbooks, threat-intelligence information and security documentation.

Analysts can provide alerts, logs or incident summaries, and the Copilot can explain the incident, identify potentially related events, summarize indicators of compromise and suggest investigation steps.

The system can classify incidents by severity, generate an investigation timeline and recommend response actions based on approved playbooks. It should provide evidence and source citations for its recommendations rather than making unsupported claims.

The Copilot will work primarily as a chatbot, allowing analysts to ask questions about security incidents using natural language.

Two Main Features

1. SOC Chatbot for Incident Investigation

The analyst can interact with the Copilot through a chatbot and ask questions such as:

What happened in this alert?

Is this activity suspicious?

What is the severity?

What are the indicators of compromise?

Which MITRE ATT&CK technique is involved?

What should I investigate next?

What response action is recommended?

The chatbot will use RAG to retrieve relevant security information before generating its answer.

2. Automatic Incident Report Generation

After analysing an incident, the Copilot can generate a structured incident report containing:

Incident summary

Incident severity

Affected user or system

Indicators of compromise

Event timeline

Possible attack technique

Evidence and sources

Investigation findings

Recommended response actions

This reduces the time required for analysts to manually prepare incident documentation.

Suggested Data

Synthetic SOC alerts

Firewall logs

Authentication logs

Endpoint logs

Network traffic summaries

Threat-intelligence reports

MITRE ATT&CK techniques

Incident-response playbooks

Security policies

Vulnerability information

Fictional incident cases

Tools and Models

Use a RAG architecture with a vector database, embeddings, an LLM, log-parsing tools, structured JSON processing and rule-based severity classification.

Useful technologies may include:

Python

FastAPI

FAISS or another vector database

Sentence Transformers

LLM / GenAI API

MITRE ATT&CK knowledge sources

React-based chatbot interface

Expected Deliverables

SOC chatbot interface

Alert and log input

Incident summarization

Severity classification

IOC extraction

Alert correlation

Incident timeline generation

MITRE ATT&CK technique mapping

Investigation recommendations

Response-playbook suggestions

RAG-based security knowledge search

Evidence/source citation

Automatic incident report generation

Evaluation KPIs

Measure:

Alert-classification accuracy

Incident-severity accuracy

IOC extraction accuracy

MITRE ATT&CK mapping acc

uracy

Retrieval relevance

Chatbot answer accuracy

Citation correctness

Incident-report completeness

Response-recommendation usefulness

Hallucination or unsupported-answer rate

Average analyst investigation time

Risks and Guardrails

The Copilot should not automatically execute destructive security actions such as deleting files, disabling accounts or blocking network infrastructure without explicit human approval.

It must clearly distinguish observed evidence from assumptions, cite the sources used for recommendations and avoid fabricating indicators or investigation results.

Sensitive logs and credentials must be protected, and the system should minimize unnecessary collection or exposure of personal and confidential information.

The chatbot should provide recommendations and assistance, while the final security decision remains with the human SOC analyst.

Overall Goal

The Cybersecurity SOC Incident-Response Copilot aims to function as a GenAI-powered chatbot assistant for SOC analysts. It helps analysts understand security alerts, investigate incidents, identify potential threats and receive evidence-based response guidance through natural-language conversation.

The system also generates structured incident reports after investigation, helping reduce manual work while keeping final security decisions under human control.
